title:
Space engineering
Ground systems and operations — Telemetry and telecommand packet utilization
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS Working Group for Ground Systems and Operations; published by ESA Publications Division)
authors: ECSS Working Group for Ground Systems and Operations
status_notes: Published 30 January 2003 as ECSS-E-70-41A ('PUS-A'). The document has no change log and states no issue number beyond the 'A' letter. Its successor is ECSS-E-ST-70-41C, the second issue of 15 April 2016 (library item ecss-e-st-70-41c-15april2016). Its change log lists ECSS-E-70-41A as the first issue and ECSS-E-70-41B as never issued (PUS-C p. 3). Footnotes on pp. 44 and 48 note that PUS version 0 was used by the earlier ESA PUS.

contents.title: Housekeeping and diagnostic data reporting service
Summary of service requests and reports
Tailoring of packet structures for a mission
Specification of the cyclic redundancy code (CRC)
Use of service type 2, device command distribution

key_points.text: PUS complements ECSS-E-50 and the CCSDS packet TM/TC recommendations by defining the application-level ground-space interface for integration, testing and flight operations.

All services are optional; each has a minimum capability set and optional additional capability sets, and PUS is a 'menu' tailored per application process and recorded in a space-ground interface control document (SGICD).
APID 2047 (all ones) is reserved by CCSDS for idle packets; PUS reserves APID 0 for the standard spacecraft time packet and requires a dedicated APID for each CPDU.
Missions may define <TCPKT_MAX_LENGTH> and <TMPKT_MAX_LENGTH> below the CCSDS 65K-octet maximum; data exceeding them use the large data transfer service with acknowledgement and retransmission.

TC packets follow CCSDS 203.0-B-2: version 0, type 1, data field header flag 1 (mandatory except for CPDU telecommands), 11-bit APID, sequence flags (11 = stand-alone), 14-bit sequence count per source and APID, packet length = data field octets - 1; maximum TC packet 65 542 octets.

TC data field header: CCSDS secondary header flag (0), TC packet PUS version number (1), Ack (4 bits: acceptance, start, progress, completion), service type (8 bits), service subtype (8 bits), optional source ID, spare; a 16-bit Packet Error Control is mandatory for TCs and its type is set by <TC_CHECKSUM_TYPE>.
Service types and subtypes 0-127 are reserved for the standard and 128-255 are mission-specific; within mission-specific services all subtypes 0-255 are free.

TM source packets follow CCSDS 102.0-B-5: type 0, data field header mandatory except for the time packet, grouping flags, 14-bit source sequence count per APID that wraps from 2^14-1 to 0 and must never 'short-cycle'.

TM data field header: spare bit, PUS version (1), spare, service type, service subtype, optional packet sub-counter, optional destination ID, optional time (CUC or CDS per <APPL_TIME_CODE>), spare; the optional 16-bit PEC is set by <TM_CHECKSUM_TYPE>.
Table 2 lists the standard service types: 1-6, 8, 9, 11-15 and 17-19; types 7, 10 and 16 are not used.

Service 1 reports: (1,1)/(1,2) acceptance success/failure, (1,3)/(1,4) execution started, (1,5)/(1,6) progress, (1,7)/(1,8) execution completed success/failure; service 2 requests: (2,1) on-off, (2,2) register load, (2,3) CPDU commands.
A parameter code is the pair PTC (parameter type code) and PFC (parameter format code); missions adopt the standard formats and may add mission-specific PFCs.

The simple parameter types are PTC 1 Boolean, 2 Enumerated, 3 Unsigned integer, 4 Signed integer, 5 Real, 6 Bit-string, 7 Octet-string, 8 Character-string, 9 Absolute time, 10 Relative time and 11 Deduced.
The packet CRC uses g(x) = x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1 with encoder and decoder initialised to all ones, computed over the whole packet except the PEC field.

Annex B mission constants include <APPL_TIME_CODE>, <CPDU_DURATION_UNIT> (10 to 15 ms), <CPDU_MAX_INSTR> (12 to 120), <MONLIST_MAX_PARAMS>, <SMALLEST_ADDRESSABLE_UNIT>, <TCPKT_MAX_LENGTH>, <TC_CHECKSUM_TYPE> and <TM_CHECKSUM_TYPE>.
Spacecraft elapsed time is a CUC count of TAI seconds from an arbitrary epoch; P-field bits 0-3 = 0010, bits 4-5 = coarse octets minus one (1-4), bits 6-7 = fine octets (0-3).

The time packet (APID 0, no data field header) carries a rate octet, then the P- and T-field time sample. The clock is sampled at the leading edge of the ASM of the VC 0 frame with VC frame count 0 (every 256 VC0 frames by default, or 128 down to 1).
A CPDU telecommand packet is 10 to 248 octets long, with an even number of octets, ends with a 16-bit CRC, and is carried in a single TC segment and frame (normally on MAP 0).

notes: This copy comes from an INAF Redmine attachment (redmine.oas.inaf.it), not from ecss.nl. The text extraction doubles hyphens in identifiers ('ECSS--E--70--41A', 'CCSDS 203.0--B--2'), so regex searches must allow for '--'. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers; PDF page 229 is blank, so srcgrep shows 229 pages while the registry gives 228. Pages 4, 6, 16, 226 and 228 are intentionally blank, and PDF page 227 is an ECSS Document Improvement Proposal form with Secretariat contact details (not reproduced here). Annex C says its text was transcribed from 'ESA PSS-04-106 Packet Telemetry Standard, Issue 1, January 1998' (p. 217), whereas ECSS-E-ST-50-03C dates that standard January 1988. The P-field table in C.2 prints '00100111' twice, where the seventh value should be '00100110' (p. 218). The normative reference ECSS-E-50 is footnoted 'To be published' (p. 15). Bit-field figures 3 and 4 extract as scrambled text (pp. 42, 46). Annex A opens with a stray 'A--A--' artefact (p. 207). The table of contents spells 'telemetr y' in Table 1 (p. 11).
